entities.summary:
Pope Felix III was the bishop of Rome from 13 March 483 to his death on 1 March 492. His repudiation of the Henotikon is considered the beginning of the Acacian schism. He is commemorated on March 1.

Felix III played a crucial role in the political landscape of the late Roman Empire, as he navigated the complex web of power struggles between the Eastern and Western Roman Empires. He also dealt with the challenges of maintaining stability in a region plagued by constant warfare and internal conflicts.

Felix III's legacy is marked by his refusal to accept the Henotikon, a document that aimed to reunite the Eastern and Western Roman Empires under a single ruler. This stance led to the division of the Roman Empire and the emergence of the Acacian schism, a significant event in the history of Christianity.

The impact of Felix III's actions can still be felt today, as his legacy continues to shape the understanding of the early Christian church and its relationship with the Roman Empire. He is remembered as a key figure in the development of the Eastern Orthodox Church and as a symbol of the enduring spirit of Christianity.

The Pope's repudiation of the Henotikon was a pivotal moment in history, marking the beginning of a new era in the relationship between the Eastern and Western Roman Empires. This event had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of European history and leaving a lasting legacy that continues to influence the world today.

Felix III's life and legacy serve as a testament to the enduring power of faith and the importance of standing up for one's beliefs, even in the face of adversity.
